assessment.answer: The score of 0.537 comes from a balance sheet that is underwater: liabilities are 158% of assets against a peer median of 64%, the current ratio is 0.43 against a peer median of 2.06, and net income swung from +$15.6M to -$232.5M with operating cash flow turning negative (-$34.0M). The filings show that this distress is real, and worse than the numbers alone suggest. The company missed an interest payment in 2023, forecast that it could not make its July 2023 interest payment, was in default before the August 2, 2023 restructuring, and says it cannot repay its roughly $705M of Credit Agreement debt if lenders demand it, while cash was about $103M at September 2022 and is mostly held abroad. The model's 4% band therefore understates the risk; the August 2023 Debt Restructuring Agreement buys time but does not fix the gap.
moved_by: Missed interest payment: the Fourth Amendment (May 2023) waived borrowing conditions so the company could draw $5.3M to pay past-due interest despite existing defaults
In July 2023 the company forecast insufficient liquidity to make its July 2023 interest payment and said it may be forced to reorganize or liquidate

Debt that cash cannot cover: about $705M of Credit Agreement borrowings expected to be classified as current at 2022 year-end, against cash of $102.9M (Sep 2022), $102.1M of it held abroad; the company says it lacks the resources to repay if demanded
The company was in default of amended covenants and had no Revolver access before August 2, 2023; filing the 10-K late was itself a covenant violation

The restructured debt is expensive (SOFR + 6.00% cash-pay loans due July 31, 2025; 14.00% PIK loans due July 31, 2027), and lender-imposed controls are tight (weekly $15M minimum U.S. liquidity, revolver draws only when U.S. cash is $7M or less)

Restructuring professionals in place: a CRO from Alvarez & Marsal and Moelis running a strategic-alternatives process; the filing names bankruptcy (reorganization or liquidation) as a possible outcome

Partly offsetting: the August 2, 2023 Debt Restructuring Agreement waived existing defaults, restored up to $21.0M of Revolver access and defers financial covenant tests to about March 31, 2024; asset sales (Indonesia, Hemingway SC, Nuvo) brought in some cash
